issues.description: The H-02 fix forces a darkAqua material base for every MXRBackdropSurface. D046 justifies this by saying every surface 'sits over the video or a dialog scrim', but that is not true for LibrarySheetView. It is presented with a native SwiftUI .sheet (MXRLibraryView.swift:47) and uses MXRBackdropSurface(tint: bgA3Transparent) with withinWindow blending. In the light theme, the rename-playlist, rename-stream and failure sheets will therefore read as a mid grey of about #A8A8A8, the same value as the bars, instead of a light surface. DialogSupport avoids this by using opaqueCounterpart in light (S39 light render is fine), but LibrarySheets does not. There is no gallery entry for it, so I could not confirm it in a render. Suggested fix: use the opaqueCounterpart in light, as DialogSupport.swift:177 does, or correct the D046 wording.

These are still not verified in the installed app: the light bars measured over real video with screencapture, Next then Esc on an isolated profile adding the folder to ml.db, and a palette tile drag using the declared UTType. When I probed, wait-idle reported the Mac in use (idle 3s), so I did not do the live part. The code paths are correct: Next calls library.addFolder right away and close() only completes onboarding. app-bundle-hook.sh adds the UTExportedTypeDeclarations entry idempotently. The offscreen S72 render gives #A8A8A8 against Figma #ABABAA.

summary:
I checked all 13 H-design findings independently. All are fixed in code and match the design evidence. One minor regression risk remains, and the live-app checks are still outstanding.

Build and tests: `swift build` is green, with no new warnings in H-design files. `gen-tokens.py --check` exits 0. ThemeContrastTests, CustomizationInteractionTests and PauseButtonContrastTests run 20 tests with 0 failures.

Findings:
- H-01 (light volume cone): the light tokens are in place. The track is #888888 (244:226) and the overlay is #FFF@0.2 (244:229). Both PlayerControls and the onboarding preview resolve them for the current colour scheme.
- H-02 (light bars): the S72.Window/light shipping-window check I ran myself shows the bars at #A8A8A8 against Figma #ABABAA (Δ3). Side by side with Figma, the bars, the compact library panel and the cone match.
- H-03 (onboarding folder): Next adds the folder immediately through MXROnboardingFolder.accept. Esc and ⌘W only complete onboarding, so the folder is kept.
- H-04 (readableSecondary): the token is removed. A grep finds no readableSecondary, keyboardFocus or App/ styles left.
- H-05 (accessibility): nsColor now honours NSWorkspace Increase Contrast through an injectable overload, and the test was rewritten to use it. Differentiate Without Color is handled in MXRIcon and in the onboarding swatches. Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast make the backdrop opaque.
- H-06 (Customize mode): my S66 hosting and S66.Window shipping-window renders match the Figma 'Player - customize' frame. The top bar is visible, the logo is not outlined, spacers have no box, play is outlined and previous is drawn normally.
- H-07 (drag UTType): the Info.plist hook declares it.
- H-08 (token hygiene): the focus ring now uses Theme.Color.fgA1, and the OSD text styles are marked as derived.
- H-09 (focus ring): the ring is drawn outside the control with a gap2 gap.
- H-10 (context menus): both sites use .mxrContextMenu.
- H-11 (onboarding layout): onboarding is now a stack layout with no scaleEffect in MXRDialogHost. S69, S70 and S71 differ from Figma only by a 0.5–2 pt offset of the bottom strip and by the D034 ⌘L keycap.
- H-12 (swatch accessibility): onboarding and Settings use the same '<X> accent' label plus the .isSelected trait.
- H-13 (metrics): the Customize and onboarding boxes are now in metrics.json. The unused standard sizes are kept on purpose, as D046 records.

Remaining issues (both minor):
- Possible regression: the dark material base is now used for every backdrop surface, including LibrarySheets. That view is a native .sheet, not drawn over the video, so light-theme rename and failure sheets probably turn mid grey. This contradicts D046's claim that every backdrop sits over the video or a scrim. There is no gallery entry for it, so I could not render it.
- I could not do the live-app checks, because the owner was using the Mac.

Outputs are in <scratch> (s72/, S66.App_customization/, S69/S70/S71 check folders, s66w.png, s39-light-*.png).
